newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU endorses deal with U.S. on Helms-Burton.
newsitem.headline: EU endorses deal with U.S. on Helms-Burton.

text.p: European Union countries on Wednesday endorsed a plan to defuse a row with the United States over U.S. anti-Cuba legislation, but accompanied it with a warning of retaliation if Washington reneges on the deal, an EU diplomat said.
"There is an agreement," the diplomat said.

Details of the agreement were not immediately available. But diplomats said earlier that France, Spain, Italy, Portugal and Belgium had been insistent on any endorsement being accompanied by a threat to reopen a World Trade Organisation disputes panel if Washington took any action against EU companies.
Ambassadors agreed on Monday to postpone the planned EU complaint against the U.S. legislation but left until Wednesday their considered reaction.

Discussions within the EU followed a deal struck between the European Commission and Washington on Friday to negotiate a compromise in policy towards Cuba, which the United States has targeted with its Helms-Burton legislation.
The Europeans have threatened high-profile action at the Geneva-based WTO in retaliation to the U.S. law, which aims to isolate the Cuban government of Fidel Castro.
